The contract tools themselves haven't gone anywhere. The contract-year chips on the Rosters page — the little blue '4' with its ticking '27d' deadline badge — were still dressed for daylight in dark mode, glowing like sticky notes on a midnight desk. They now wear proper dark-mode colors: translucent fills, readable text, and a deadline badge that shifts from amber to orange to red as the clock runs down without searing your retinas on the way.

The card now wears the standard player-cell chip: team-color gradient backdrop, spotlight behind the head, team-tinted ring in both themes. Bijan glows Falcons red on the card, same as he does in the list. Defenses keep their clean logo treatment. The Draft Order page now knows what phase of the calendar it lives in. During the season it's a live prediction that moves with the standings; once the champion is crowned and the toilet bowl comp picks are settled, it wears an official badge instead of hedging; and now that the rookie draft is in the books, it says so plainly — final order as drafted, with the next prediction cycle firing up when the new season kicks off. The spring draft heroes got the same memo and link to 'View Draft Order' instead of a predictor that stopped predicting months ago.

Design System & Theming — Light mode finally got the memo about team colors. The ring around each chip is cut from the same cloth, mixed darker in light mode so it frames the chip against a white page, lighter in dark mode so it pops off a black one. Bo Nix glows Broncos orange at noon and at midnight. The dark-mode player-headshot fix from earlier today found four stragglers. The live-scoring scoreboard was mixing its own paint — player chips built from raw team colors with none of the brightness safeguards, so a Titan or Steeler could still vanish into a midnight circle mid-game. The Projected Free Agents table and the AFL player pool had quietly skipped team colors entirely, showing plain gray chips in dark mode while their sibling pages got the full treatment. And the Rosters page's players-by-team and players-by-college cards were hand-sewing their own player rows without the backdrop. All four now use the same spotlight-behind-the-head backdrop as everywhere else, plus a half-opacity white ring that lifts every chip off the dark page. A new build-time guard makes it structural: any future page that hand-rolls its own team-color-behind-a-player math — or renders a player chip without the backdrop — fails the build and gets pointed at the shared helper. One paintbrush, whole site. Dark mode stopped hiding half the league's rookies. The little circular player headshots wear their NFL team's colors behind them — great in theory, except a third of the league (Titans, Steelers, Bears, Seahawks, Texans...) wears colors that are basically midnight, so a guy like Cam Ward in a navy jersey on a navy chip on a dark page was just a rumor of a face. The chips now reach for each team's lighter brand color when the main one is too dark — Titans light blue, Steelers gold, Bears orange — and every chip puts a soft spotlight right where the player's head sits, brightest behind the face and deepening toward the rim. Every team's backdrop is held to a minimum brightness, enforced by a build-time guard so no future team-color tweak can sink a headshot back into the void. Light mode untouched; it was never the problem. Dark mode got a full sweep of the closet. The Admin Hub bug from earlier this week — styling against color tokens that don't actually exist, so everything silently rendered its light-mode fallback — turned out to have cousins in some forty files: white draft-queue rows on a dark draft room, lineup accordions and matchup pickers stuck with light text, homepage urgency chips glowing like flashlights, and a templates page whose headings had no color at all. Every one now runs through the real theme tokens, and a new build-time guard fails any future code that references a token that doesn't exist — so this whole class of bug is done recurring.

Navigation & Routing — The side menu's league-switch chevron now actually switches leagues. On theleague.us and afl-fantasy.com it used to strip the other league's address right out of its own link — so 'Switch to AFL' just reloaded the page you were already on. It now carries you straight to the same page on the other league's site, and the chevron shows for everyone instead of hiding unless you were logged in as a dual-league owner.

Admin — The Admin Hub finally respects dark mode — its cards were stuck glowing white on the dark background because they styled themselves against token names that don't exist — and the August Cutdown Report now has a card there, so the commissioner's audit trail is one click away instead of a memorized URL.

Standings — Standings finally sit still on your phone — the Premier League tables (and every other standings view) used to shove the whole page sideways, so you had to swipe left and right just to read a record. Now the columns that matter — rank, team, and record — fit the screen, the rest tuck away until you've got the width for them, and the desktop layout is untouched.

title: Introducing Best Ball #1: Draft Once, Never Set a Lineup Again
summary: A third league joins the family — 12 teams, one 25-round startup draft run entirely on this site, and then absolutely nothing to manage. No waivers, no lineups, no trades. Draft well or wear it all season. The draft room is built, the mock lobby is open, and the clock is waiting.
description: Some leagues are marriages. TheLeague, with its contracts and cap sheets and August cut deadlines, is a marriage. Best Ball #1 is a first date that decides your entire year: one night, 25 rounds, 300 picks, and then you put the roster down and never touch it again. Your best scorers start themselves every week. That's the whole format. That's the whole league.

The main event runs right here on the site — the same live draft room engine that powers mock drafts, promoted to the real thing. Draft board, full veteran player pool sorted by redraft ADP (this is a win-now league; nobody's drafting for 2029), a pick queue, trash-talk chat, and an on-the-clock timer with an auto-pick safety net for whoever's getting a snack when their turn comes up. When the last pick lands, the results get imported to MyFantasyLeague and the season simply… runs.

Until draft night, the practice facility is open: the mock draft lobby spins up full 25-round rehearsals against the clock, and the Import Rankings page pulls your board in from FantasyPros or FootballGuys to power your queue. The rules fit on one page — which is the point. Draft once. Watch football. Argue about it in the chat. See you on the clock.
imageAlt: The Best Ball #1 league home: emerald hero announcing the 2026 startup draft with cards for the Draft Room, Draft Board, and Rosters.

title: The Cut List Is Now Yours to Boss Around
summary: Drag any player — even the machine's picks — into your cut order, unmark with one click, and watch a red dashed CUT LINE split who goes from who's safe. Oh, and the panel saves itself now, which beats its old habit of quietly forgetting your work.
description: First, a confession from the beat desk: until this week, the Cutdown Plan panel had a split personality. You'd mark your August cuts, watch the slate update beautifully — and then saving would post your original list and reset everything, like a waiter who nods through your whole order and brings you what the last table had. That bug is dead. And so is the Save button, because the panel now saves itself about a second after you stop fiddling — the status line tells you the moment your cuts are locked in, and it means it.

With the trust rebuilt, the slate got handed over to you completely. Every row is draggable now, not just your own picks — grab one of the machine's LAST ADDED selections, drop it where you want it, and it becomes YOUR PICK at that exact spot. On your phone, a Mark button does the same job with a tap, and every marked player wears an × so you can change your mind without opening his player card.

Best of all: marking more players than the deadline needs no longer hides the overflow. Everybody renders in one ordered list, split by a red dashed CUT LINE — players above it go on deadline night, players below it are your insurance, safe unless the roster grows. The numbering runs straight across the line, arrows and drags cross it freely, and even when you're at the limit with nothing to cut, your order stays visible and waiting. The automation still swings the axe. You just fully control the order of the chopping block.
imageAlt: The Cutdown Plan slate with three marked cuts above a red dashed cut line and a fourth marked player parked safely below it.

title: Your Roster Now Tells You Who's Getting Cut
summary: Over the 22-man limit? Your roster rows now wear the cut slate on their sleeves — gold AUTO-CUT badges in the exact order the deadline job will swing the axe. Mark nobody and it flags your newest pickups; mark your own and the badges flip to YOUR PICK.
description: Last month the Cutdown Plan panel promised the machine had your back at the deadline — "last players in are the first ones out." True, but abstract. A policy isn't a picture. Now it's a picture. Open your roster during the cut window and the players headed for the chopping block wear it right next to their name: a gold AUTO-CUT #1, #2, #3 badge, laid out in the exact order the automation will make the cuts.

Here's the part that matters: you don't have to mark a single player to see this. Marked nothing? The roster fills the slate with your most recent waiver and free-agent pickups and stamps each one LAST ADDED — because that's the tiebreaker the deadline job actually uses (and yes, players you traded for are safe; a deadline-week acquisition doesn't count as "just added"). Start marking your own casualties and those badges flip to YOUR PICK and jump to the front of the line. Same math, honest labels — AUTO-CUT for whoever's inside the cut line right now, MARKED for the insurance picks sitting safely below it.

A legend under the table does the accounting out loud — how many players are getting cut, and the night it happens — with a standing invitation to choose your own instead. Because the automation will happily pick for you. It's just picking by recency, not by heart. See exactly who's on the block, then go tell it who should be.
imageAlt: Roster rows during the August cut window with four players wearing gold AUTO-CUT #1 through #4 · LAST ADDED badges beside their contract years and salaries.
